headline: Public transcriptomes yield prognostic gene signatures and immune-linked candidate targets
label: Integrative Multi Omics Target Prioritization
summary: Bulk transcriptome-based target prioritization is being paired with experimental validation and exposure biology across diverse solid tumors and disease models.
synthesis: The dominant thread is in silico target prioritization on public bulk transcriptomes from TCGA or GEO, using LASSO-based Cox or LASSO models and WGCNA to derive prognostic signatures, often with scRNA-seq and immune infiltration estimates. Several studies validate signatures in external cohorts, including CGGA for glioblastoma and GSE42127 for lung adenocarcinoma, and some add Mendelian randomization. Not every item follows this template. A two-stage deep learning framework (NN+SVR, IG+SVR) selects genes from esophageal adenocarcinoma bulk RNA-seq and outperforms LIMMA and SAM, while a graph neural network screen prioritizes TP53, CDH1 and APC variants in gastric cancer. What is new is the layering of experimental validation and exposure biology onto hub-gene selection, as in MATR3 and RAPGEF2 work, microplastic-exposed colitis with PI3K-Akt signaling, and a 6PPDQ network toxicology study.
